title: Az-Zalzalah again: the earth's report
hookLine: the ground itself will tell what was done on it (99:4–5)

cards: Archaeologists can read a floor. Dig down through a site, and the dirt tells you who lived there, what they ate, where they cooked, when the fire came. A footprint pressed into mud can outlast the person who made it.
The ground keeps records nobody asked it to keep. Today, back to the line in the middle of Surah az-Zalzalah, the one skipped yesterday: the earth itself as a witness.
And a new stretch of the path begins, the middle surahs, a little longer, a little deeper.

teach.b: On that Day, after the quake, the surah says the earth speaks.
In Pickthall's translation: That day she will relate her chronicles, Because thy Lord inspireth her.

teach.h: SHE TESTIFIES TO WHAT WAS DONE ON HER.
teach.b: Chronicles, akhbar: news, reports, the story of what happened. The earth everyone has walked on will give its account. How?

The surah's answer is simple: because the Lord inspires her, tells her to. A hadith in Tirmidhi fills in the picture. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ recited this verse and asked his companions: do you know what her news is?

They said: Allah and His Messenger know best. He said: her news is that she will testify about every servant, man or woman, about what they did on her back. She'll say: he did this, on such and such a day.
So every place is a witness. The kitchen where you were patient, or weren't. The sidewalk where you stepped around someone, or stopped.
The office, the car, the park bench.

Some scholars drew a gentle conclusion: pray in different places, so more of the earth can speak well of you. Some pray the extra prayers in a different spot from the obligatory ones, partly for this reason.
Notice the tone. The ground isn't an enemy, spying. It's more like an old friend who was there the whole time, and it can remember good as easily as harm.

how: Some Muslims pray their voluntary prayers in a different spot from the obligatory ones, and scholars have connected the practice with the earth bearing witness on the Day of Judgment.

o: the harvest a farmer gathers in autumn
the spring rain that turns the desert green
the earth telling what was done on it

games.q: what's inside the verse — tap the pairs.
p: what was done on her back
more ground to speak for you

s: the surah says the earth will speak on that Day
she will relate her chronicles, because her Lord inspires her (99:4–5).
in the hadith, the earth only reports wrongs
she testifies to what each person did on her; the hadith doesn't limit it to wrongs.
the Prophet asked his companions what the earth's news is
then answered: she will testify about what each did on her back (Tirmidhi).

games.q: the Prophet recites the verse and asks: do you know what her news is? what do the companions answer?
o: Allah and His Messenger know best
the news of the end of time
games.why: they deferred, and he told them: she will testify about every servant, about what they did on her back (Tirmidhi).

practice: Stand if you can, or rest your feet flat on the floor, and notice the ground holding you; ask what this spot has seen from you this week.
Then take ten slow steps, as if the ground could feel each one and would remember how you walked. If you can't walk, press your feet softly into the floor, ten times.
